note: Gap-fill only, keyed by the stable ids in data/waypoint-ids.json. This file deliberately covers just the waypoints that carried no description in the source data; the 29 main-list waypoints and 3 off-track waypoints that already carry first-hand field notes are absent here and keep them, which is the point — those notes are primary data, and descriptions.json overrides source text. Applied by scripts/build-trails.ts and uploadable to the comments API with scripts/upload-descriptions.ts. Listed north to south, matching the km order of the generated trail data, with off-track waypoints appended at the end.

descriptions.name: Cooma Cottage
descriptions.description: Historic homestead just outside Yass, once Hamilton Hume's home and now the northern end of the track that carries his name. The walk starts here and runs south to Albury.

descriptions.name: Yass caravan park
descriptions.description: Caravan park on the edge of Yass, the first camping and showers after Cooma Cottage. Yass itself has shops and food.

descriptions.name: Crown rest site
descriptions.description: Rest site on crown land in the farmland country south of Yass. A simple place to stop or shelter, with no facilities or water marked.

descriptions.name: Billy Grace reserve
descriptions.description: Riverside camping reserve near Wee Jasper, on the flats beside the Goodradigbee. Open ground close to the Fitzpatrick trackhead; the water is untreated river water.

descriptions.name: Brindabella road
descriptions.description: Crossing of Brindabella Road in the mountain country west of Canberra. It is a winding, mostly unsealed road with light traffic, and is reachable by vehicle for lifts and food drops.

descriptions.name: Browns creek
descriptions.description: Creekside campsite in the hills above the Blowering valley. Basic bush camping, with the creek as the water source — untreated, and low late in a dry season.

descriptions.name: CLOSED C - Ben Smith campsite
descriptions.description: Flagged as closed in the track data. NPWS and Hume and Hovell Track notices carry the current status of campsites through this section.

descriptions.name: Paddys river dam actual
descriptions.description: The corrected position for the Paddys River Dam campsite, about a kilometre along the track from the other pin of the same name. The two pins are the same site.

descriptions.name: Wymah road start
descriptions.description: Where the track joins Wymah Road for a road section of roughly eight kilometres, ending at the matching Wymah road end marker. The road is open to traffic and walked on the verge.

descriptions.name: lake Hume turnoff
descriptions.description: Turnoff toward Lake Hume and the caravan park on its shore, the main accommodation in this part of the walk. Opening seasons and booking arrangements vary.

descriptions.name: Wymah road end
descriptions.description: The track leaves Wymah Road here and returns to trail, closing out the road section that began at the Wymah road start marker.

descriptions.name: C? Bowna rest area
descriptions.description: Rest area near Bowna on the Lake Hume side of the track. The question mark in the name flags that camping here is unconfirmed.

descriptions.name: Cafe and takeaway
descriptions.description: Cafe and takeaway as the track comes in toward Albury, the last food before the finish. Opening hours vary.

descriptions.name: Hovell tree
descriptions.description: The southern end of the track: the river red gum beside the Murray at Albury that William Hovell marked on the 1824 expedition. It stands in a riverside park, with the town's full services close by.

descriptions.name: Tumut valley holiday park
descriptions.description: Holiday park in Tumut, off the track and the usual base for a town night through this section — showers, beds and powered sites, with the town's shops for resupply. Sites fill over holiday periods.

descriptions.name: Restaurant area
descriptions.description: An off-track pin marking an eating area rather than a named venue. Opening days are limited in the small places along this stretch.
